core_obligations: The transfinite construction (proof lines 1721-1750): following the proof the author invites the reader to compare with, the objects attached to an ordinal are built by a transfinite recursion that inserts, at each successor step, an extension killing a morphism out of a subobject of a standard object, and takes colimits at limit ordinals.

Termination (proof lines 1750-1755): the smallness of the objects involved ensures that the construction stabilises at some ordinal, so the assignment is defined for every object and is functorial in it.

Injectivity (proof lines 1755-1759): an extension problem for the stabilised object is solved by the construction of the next step, so the object satisfies the injectivity criterion and is therefore injective.
proof_roadmap: Run the transfinite construction that kills one morphism at a time.
Use smallness to stop the process.
Apply the injectivity criterion to the stabilised object, and observe functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that every Grothendieck abelian category has functorial injective embeddings (statement lines 1715-1719). The proof is a complete argument: the author runs a transfinite construction that adjoins, at each successor ordinal, a solution of one extension problem, taking colimits at limit ordinals (proof lines 1721-1750); smallness makes the process stop, which yields a functorially defined object (proof lines 1750-1755); and the stabilised object satisfies the injectivity criterion because the next step of the construction would solve any extension problem (proof lines 1755-1759). The non-formal content is the transfinite construction and its termination. The claim is H3.
